title: The Tenant Below
synopsis: Your first night in the new apartment, a note slides under your door: please stop dragging the chair at 3 a.m. You don't own a chair. And it isn't 3 a.m. yet.

nodes.text: You have not unpacked a single box. You have not made a single sound. Still, at 9 p.m. on your first night, a folded note whispers under the door in tidy handwriting: Please stop dragging the chair at 3 a.m. It's every night now. — 3B. You do not own a chair.

choices.consequence: You commit to slip a polite note back. It carries you into Correspondence while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to go downstairs and knock on 3B. It carries you into Apartment 3B while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You write: New tenant, no chair, so sorry — must be the pipes. By morning a reply waits: The chair again last night. And now the humming, that low tune you do. Please. You have never hummed in this apartment. You buy a secondhand chair that afternoon without letting yourself ask why.

choices.text: Test it — drag the chair at 3 a.m. on purpose
choices.consequence: You commit to test it — drag the chair at 3 a.m. on purpose. It carries you into 3:00 A.M. while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Keep the apartment silent all night
choices.consequence: You choose to keep the apartment silent all night. By The Silent Night, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: No one answers the knock, but the door is chained from inside and a voice comes through the gap — thin, kind, exhausted. "Oh," it says, as if you have arrived somewhere it did not expect you yet. "You're early.

choices.text: Ask what they mean by early
choices.consequence: You ask what they mean by early. The way toward Early opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You choose to leave, and never knock again. By The Silent Night, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You wait up. At 2:59 you grip the chair, and at 3:00 exactly you drag it hard across the floor. The note is already there. It has been there for hours, timestamped, describing this precise scrape, this precise minute — and one line more, at the bottom, waiting for you to catch up to it.

choices.text: Read the next line and follow it
choices.consequence: You commit to read the next line and follow it. It carries you into Early while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Burn the notes and start packing
choices.consequence: You choose to burn the notes and start packing. By The Lease Breaks You, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You make no sound at all. You breathe through your mouth. You do not so much as shift your weight. And at 3 a.m. the note comes anyway: Thank you for trying. But you should know — it was never you making the sounds. It's the floor. It practices.

choices.text: Stay awake to catch the real source
choices.consequence: You commit to stay awake to catch the real source. It carries you into What Makes the Sounds while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Set a packed bag by the door, just in case
choices.consequence: You commit to set a packed bag by the door, just in case. It carries you into The Lease Breaks You while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: "The building runs a night ahead of the people in it," 3B says. "The notes aren't complaints. They're warnings. I'm you — a night further on than you are now — sliding them back so you'll know what you're about to do before you do it.

choices.consequence: You choose to start writing notes forward yourself. By Tomorrow's Neighbor, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You refuse to play along. The way toward What Makes the Sounds opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You find it at last, in the space between the floors: the building rehearsing its tenants — every scrape and hum and footstep of everyone who ever lived here or ever will, all at once, learning to sound lived-in. It notices you noticing. It would like you to be a very good tenant.

choices.text: Join the rehearsal; become part of the house
choices.consequence: You choose to join the rehearsal; become part of the house. By A Very Good Tenant, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You break the pattern and run. The way toward The Lease Breaks You opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You leave before your second night, boxes still taped, deposit forfeited. Weeks later you drive past and see a light in your old window and a new name on the buzzer. You mail them a single note, tidy and unsigned: Please don't drag the chair at 3 a.m. It never stops.

You take up the pen and the chain and the long patient watch. Now you are the voice through the gap in 3B, a night ahead, slipping warnings backward to whoever moves in next — hoping, each time, that this one reads them early enough to leave.

You stop resisting, and the house is so grateful. You are quiet now, wonderfully quiet, folded into its long memory with all the others. Sometimes, when a new tenant lies awake upstairs, you help with the sounds. You are, everyone agrees, a very good tenant.
